Figure 2: Top: illustrative examples of different conditional and counterfactual distributions (PY |A=1,PY (1)). Although covariate overlap is weak (top left), PY |A=1 and PY (1) share the same support and tails (as predicted by Theorem 3.1), and are statistically much closer than the covariate mixing distributions (as predicted by (2)). Bottom: the optimal transport maps between these distributions are more regular and closer to the identity map than transport from N (0, 1) (there is no bijective flow from N2(0, I) in the simplex-valued case).
